scenarios.name: Moderate downturn
scenarios.rationale: A moderate fall in volumes lowers earnings from the {{FIG:ebitda_ltm|US$ m}} twelve-month level while debt of {{FIG:total_debt_ltm|US$ m}} and cash interest stay as reported.

scenarios.name: Severe downturn
scenarios.rationale: A severe fall in volumes cuts earnings by a larger share of the {{FIG:ebitda_ltm|US$ m}} twelve-month level; debt and cash interest stay as reported.

scenarios.name: Severe downturn with higher rates
scenarios.rationale: The severe fall in volumes coincides with a rise in the rate paid on the term loan.
scenarios.limitation: No rate curve or hedging disclosure supports the size of the interest increase.

scenarios.name: Total loss of earnings
scenarios.rationale: A boundary case in which earnings fall to zero; it shows which ratios stop being meaningful and which stay calculable.

thresholds.label: Total leverage watch level
thresholds.rationale: An internal watch level, not a covenant; no covenant source is bound to this run.

thresholds.label: Net leverage watch level
thresholds.rationale: An internal watch level, not a covenant; no covenant source is bound to this run.

thresholds.label: Interest coverage watch level
thresholds.rationale: An internal watch level, not a covenant; no covenant source is bound to this run.

assessment.rationale: The credit starts from total leverage of {{FIG:total_leverage_reported|x}}, net leverage of {{FIG:net_leverage_reported|x}}, interest coverage of {{FIG:interest_coverage_reported|x}} and free cash flow of {{FIG:fcf_ltm|US$ m}}; the scenarios test how far earnings can fall before those measures reach the watch levels.
assessment.limitation: Scenario sizes and watch levels are analyst assumptions.

gaps.gap: No covenant document or maturity schedule is an input to this stress.
gaps.why_it_matters: The watch levels are the analyst's, so the order in which lenders' own tests are reached may differ from the order shown.
gaps.action: Run the covenant owner and compare its tests with the watch levels.
